journal.landing.heading: A daily journal you can search by meaning
journal.landing.line: Windmill Journal is one continuous page: tonight’s entry under yesterday’s, with the cursor already waiting. Nothing replies, and nothing counts the days.
journal.landing.trust: No account needed. Signed out, your pages stay in this browser.
journal.landing.echoes.title: Your own words, {break}echoed back
journal.landing.echoes.paragraph: Once you have a free account and twenty written pages, saving a page can bring back passages you wrote before on the same thing, each with its date.
journal.landing.echoes.wordsText: What returns is your own earlier writing. No model writes a reply.
journal.landing.echoes.homeText: Open an echo to read the page it came from, then come back.
journal.landing.echoes.freeText: A hosted model finds echoes. Windmill pays for them, and they do not count against your AI amount.
journal.landing.echoes.line: On a wide screen echoes sit beside the page, and on a narrow one behind a tab. In the iPhone beta they are a count that opens a sheet.
journal.landing.search.title: Find what you wrote, {break}without the exact words
journal.landing.search.paragraph: Type a feeling or a subject. Search matches pages by meaning and opens the passage in place, with its neighbours around it.
journal.landing.search.deviceText: The model, the index and what you type stay in your browser.
journal.landing.search.wordsText: Exact matches answer at once, then meaning reorders them.
journal.landing.search.webText: Search is not in the iPhone beta.
journal.landing.page.title: One page {break}a night
journal.landing.page.paragraph: Every day sits on one scroll, oldest at the top and today at the bottom. There are no titles, folders, tags or prompts.
journal.landing.page.savesText: A save that fails says so and keeps your words.
journal.landing.page.yesterdayText: Today is the page you write. Past days are for reading.
journal.landing.back.title: Look back {break}without a score
journal.landing.back.paragraph: Zoom out to see your months and the year. A day you did not write is drawn as a gap, not as a miss.
journal.landing.back.weekText: Days written and words, as plain counts.
journal.landing.back.scalesTitle: Mood and energy, if you want
journal.landing.back.scalesText: Two optional scales from 0 to 10. Zero is a real answer, and blank is fine.
journal.landing.back.praiseText: Nothing congratulates a high value or flags a low one.
journal.landing.back.line: Zoom, the week and the two scales are on the web.
journal.landing.quiet.title: Nothing {break}writes back
journal.landing.quiet.paragraph: Windmill Journal never interprets what you wrote, gives advice or asks you questions. It is a page, not a companion.
journal.landing.quiet.streaksText: No streak, no percentage and no count of missed days.
journal.landing.quiet.promptsText: Nothing is required before you can write.
journal.landing.quiet.shareText: There is no way to share a page. The control does not exist.
journal.landing.data.title: What stays on your device, {break}and what does not
journal.landing.data.paragraph: Signed out, your pages stay in this browser or on your phone. Signed in, Windmill stores your pages so they follow your account, and each save of changed text is sent to Anthropic to find echoes.
journal.landing.data.localText: A search never leaves your device.
journal.landing.data.termsText: It does not train on your pages by default and deletes them within 30 days. No zero-retention agreement is in place.
journal.landing.data.doorText: Journal is the one room an outside assistant cannot reach.
journal.landing.keep.title: Yours to keep, {break}and where it runs
journal.landing.keep.paragraph: With an account, export every page as one Markdown file, oldest first. Windmill Journal runs in a web browser, and in an iPhone beta that is not public yet.
journal.landing.keep.leaveText: Closing your account erases your pages after 30 days.
journal.landing.keep.talkText: Speak a page and it is written down. Talk needs Windmill One, which is not on sale yet.
journal.landing.keep.roomsText: Windmill Roadmap for a plan, Windmill Gym for training. One account for all three.
journal.landing.questions.title: Questions
journal.landing.questions.findQuestion: How do I find something I wrote if I don’t remember the words?
journal.landing.questions.findAnswer: Describe it. Search matches pages by meaning and runs in your browser, on your device.
journal.landing.questions.rereadQuestion: Should I reread my old journal?
journal.landing.questions.rereadAnswer: You do not have to schedule it. Once you are signed in and have twenty written pages, earlier passages on the same thing can appear beside a page after you save it.
journal.landing.questions.missQuestion: What happens if I miss a day?
journal.landing.questions.missAnswer: Nothing. There is no streak and no count of missed days.
journal.landing.questions.replyQuestion: Does the journal write back or ask me questions?
journal.landing.questions.replyAnswer: No. What appears beside a page is your own earlier writing, not a reply.
journal.landing.questions.privateAnswer: There is no share control, and search runs on your device. When you are signed in, finding echoes sends the text of a saved page to Anthropic.
journal.landing.questions.freeQuestion: Can I journal online for free without signing up?
journal.landing.questions.freeAnswer: Yes. Signed out, your pages stay in this browser on this device. Echoes need a free account.
journal.landing.questions.aiAnswer: Search uses a small model that runs in your browser. Echoes use a hosted model from Anthropic, for signed-in writers only.
journal.landing.lookBack.legend: Hollow means nothing written. Counted at nobody.
journal.landing.night.earlier: Rain stopped around eight; the street smelled like summer for a minute.
journal.landing.night.echo: Walked back past the bakery for no reason except the light. Some detours are the point.
journal.landing.night.tonight: Took the long way home. The kitchen still smelled of coffee, and the light on the counter was worth the extra ten minutes.
journal.landing.searchSheet.foot: Opening a hit flies the canvas to the spot — neighbours intact, never a detail view.
journal.landing.searchSheet.friLine: Everyone at dinner seemed further along. I kept comparing timelines instead of tasting anything.
journal.landing.searchSheet.thuLine: Made the good soup for no occasion.
journal.landing.write.yesterdayLine: …I could hear what I’d been chewing on all week.
